title: Bologna Sandwich on White Bread with Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A Bologna sandwich on white bread with cheese is a classic fast‑food item made of sliced boiled Bologna sausage, melted cheese, and a soft white roll. It is popular in cafeterias and cafés for its quick preparation and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Bologna” comes from the Italian city of Bologna, although the Russian version has a different recipe.
The sandwich is often served hot: the cheese melts and the bread is lightly toasted, enhancing the aroma.
In the Soviet era a similar sandwich was called a “bread with sausage and cheese,” but today it is considered a distinct product.
White bread gives a soft texture, but it can be swapped for whole‑grain for a healthier option.
The sandwich is frequently included in children’s menus because it is easy to digest and provides protein.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Both the sausage and cheese supply complete proteins essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese provides calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The bread’s carbohydrates quickly replenish energy stores.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bologna sausage is rich in B1, B2, and B12 vitamins, which aid nervous system function.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture makes the sandwich suitable for children and people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and sausage contain saturated fats that should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some Bologna sausages contain nitrites and other preservatives that are best consumed in moderation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy should avoid the cheese component.

items.title: High glycemic index of white bread
items.content: White bread can cause a rapid spike in blood sugar levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be enjoyed hot or cold. For a hot version, toast it in a pan or toaster until the cheese is golden. Serve with a side salad, pickles, or mustard.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sandwich in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Store the sausage and cheese separately in airtight packaging, and keep the bread in a dry place to prevent it from becoming stale.
